Suppose the finite poset $P$ satisfies the upper-interval criterion of G.9. For $Z=\|NP\|$ and its minimum map $s:Z\to P$, the spectral transform has the identification \[ V_P\simeq s_+\,\mathbb V_Z\,s^*. \tag{G.12} \] Here $\mathbb V_Z$ is Lurie's covariant sheaf--cosheaf duality and $s_+$ is cosheaf pushforward, with value on $U$ given by the value on $s^{-1}U$. The same identification holds for derived coefficients over a ring. Thus it includes an explicit pushforward of cosheaves; it does not require the ordinary sheaf-valued Verdier dual to stay constructible for the same minimum strata. A concrete class satisfying the criterion is $P=\operatorname{Face}(K)^{\mathrm{op}}$ for any finite simplicial complex $K$, with nonempty faces. In this case the minimum strata on the barycentric subdivision are precisely the open simplices of $K$, so the identification is the usual cellular geometric one. | claim (return: Known) | Part G positive geometric identification |

/workspace/scratch/cb96d9ba0f27/context/companion/chunks/DER_XIIc-b.tex:399:The relevant meaning of $W$-fibration is likewise intrinsic to $W$. Precisely, for $p:X\to Y$, the pullback functor $p^*:\mathcal M/Y\to\mathcal M/X$ must preserve the arrows whose underlying maps belong to $W$. This also implies the same assertion after another base change. This is the property used below, together with the stability of these maps under composition and pullback. In particular, one must not replace $\mathrm{Fib}_W$ by the fibrations of an arbitrary model structure without checking the corresponding properness statement. Here ``weakly saturated'' means that $W$ contains the isomorphisms and satisfies two-out-of-three; it does not mean that every arrow inverted by localization already belongs to $W$. A factorization $f=pi$ with $i\in W$ and $p\in\mathrm{Fib}_W$ is sufficient for the replacement operations that are actually written down; it is not, by its form alone, a pair of lifting axioms.

title: Why Δ opposite is neither weak nor local test
note: Verification of the lead credited to Hua: if a small category A has an initial object 0, the category of elements A/X of any presheaf decomposes by X(0), each component having initial object (0,x), so all its represented homotopy types are discrete. Consequently A cannot be weak test, and each slice A/a again has an initial object, so A is not local test either; apply this to A=Δᵒᵖ, whose initial object is [0], to exclude test and strict test as well. Confidence: high, because this is a direct category-of-elements argument with the weak/local definitions, not a claim of novelty.

/workspace/scratch/cb96d9ba0f27/context/DOSSIER_STATEMENTS_WITH_STATUS.md:225:| BISITE G.12 | A correct geometric Verdier identification with a checked hypothesis. Suppose the finite poset $P$ satisfies the upper-interval criterion of G.9. For $Z=\|NP\|$ and its minimum map $s:Z\to P$, the spectral transform has the identification \[ V_P\simeq s_+\,\mathbb V_Z\,s^*. \tag{G.12} \] Here $\mathbb V_Z$ is Lurie's covariant sheaf--cosheaf duality and $s_+$ is cosheaf pushforward, with value on $U$ given by the value on $s^{-1}U$. The same identification holds for derived coefficients over a ring. Thus it includes an explicit pushforward of cosheaves; it does not require the ordinary sheaf-valued Verdier dual to stay constructible for the same minimum strata. A concrete class satisfying the criterion is $P=\operatorname{Face}(K)^{\mathrm{op}}$ for any finite simplicial complex $K$, with nonempty faces. In this case the minimum strata on the barycentric subdivision are precisely the open simplices of $K$, so the identification is the usual cellular geometric one. | claim (return: Known) | Part G positive geometric identification |

/workspace/scratch/cb96d9ba0f27/context/DOSSIER_STATEMENTS_WITH_STATUS.md:278:| RESIDUE F.7 | Universal Cat-colimit shapes without a weakly terminal object. For a connected countable category $I$ without a weakly terminal object, and hence also in general, the implication from the universal ordinary-Cat-colimit comparison to filteredness remains unresolved here. F.4 gives a necessary totality condition and the full weakly-terminal case. The unbounded injective-ordinal examples do not refute this implication: the diagram $[n]\mapsto B\mathbb N^{n+1}$ has categorical colimit $B\mathbb N\simeq S^1$, whereas its Grothendieck construction has integral homology $\mathbb Z$ in every degree. On all of $\Delta_{\rm inj}$ its degree-$k$ fibre homology, for $k\geq1$, is the projective representable $\mathbb Z[\Delta_{\rm inj}([k-1],-)]$; the homotopy-colimit spectral sequence collapses. On an arbitrary unbounded full subcategory $A_S$, the restricted diagram need not be representable. Instead its higher derived colimits vanish by exactness in F.3, and its colimit is $\mathbb Z$: any two marked $k$-element ordered subsets admit embeddings into a common larger ordinal identifying their marks, then into an object of $A_S$. The categorical colimit is still $B\mathbb N$, since the same embeddings identify all coordinate generators and introduce precisely their commutative-monoid relation. Thus all these shapes fail the premise. This prevents importing the nonfiltered total example as an answer to the different Cat-colimit question. | claim (return: Open) |  |

The new numbering must be kept separate from both the preceding pages and present-day derivator terminology. Here \textbf{Der 3} asserts that a contractible indexing category has fully faithful constant-diagram functor. The two parts of \textbf{Der 4} assert existence of right and left Kan extensions; the two parts of \textbf{Der 5} give their pointwise comma-category formulas. /workspace/scratch/cb96d9ba0f27/context/companion/chunks/DER_I-b.tex:96:The new contractibility axiom is not an assertion that the whole category $\D(X)$ collapses to $\D(e)$. It concerns only constant objects and their morphisms. For example, over the walking arrow a coefficient is a coherent arrow, and its two values need not be isomorphic even though the walking arrow has contractible nerve. What the axiom guarantees is that taking a constant object over this shape introduces no new endomorphisms. This is precisely the amount of invariance used when the lifting categories in the following theorem are contractible.

title: The recognition claim is too broad for ordinary projectives
note: The criterion says “assez de projectifs”, then permits P=UlProj, but ordinary projectives do not suffice: published Grothendieck-category counterexamples have enough projectives without a small family of compact projective generators. Saorín–Šťovíček §5 explicitly includes the many-object module-category setting, and Bazzoni et al. Corollary4.5/Theorem6.3 provide the original tilting-heart construction, with the many-object bridge checked in the secondary review. Thus the assertion is false under the ordinary meaning of projective; a small generating family of compact/ultraprojective objects is the additional condition, while any strengthened meaning of the manuscript word remains an editorial interpretation.

No restriction to finite posets is necessary for admissibility once the relevant ordinary Kan extension and uniform diagram structures exist. title: The projectivity corollary
note: The corollary asserts that projective L and projective x give projective L⊗x. In an additive cocomplete M, epimorphisms are exactly maps with zero cokernel, so epimorphisms in the additive functor category are pointwise; projectivity of x then gives a pointwise surjection after applying Hom_M(x,−), and projectivity of L completes the lifting through the displayed Hom adjunction. This is an own elementary verification with high confidence from that lifting argument: no abelian hypothesis is needed for this particular corollary, although the subsequent Tor and derived discussion requires its separately stated exactness hypotheses.

Define \[ \operatorname{Fib}_W=\{p:E\to B\mid p^*: \mathcal M/B\to\mathcal M/E\text{ sends }W_B\text{ into }W_E\}. \] Thus every test is an arrow $v:T'\to T$ over $B$, with arbitrary structure map $T\to B$, and the tested arrow is $E\times_B T'\to E\times_B T$. This class contains isomorphisms and is closed under composition and arbitrary pullback. These assertions require no two-out-of-three axiom. Let $A\subseteq W$ contain isomorphisms and be composition-closed, and let $L$ contain isomorphisms and be pullback-closed. Define \[ \begin{split} T_W(A)&=\{p:E\to B\mid p^*\text{ sends every arrow of }A \text{ in }\mathcal M/B\text{ into }W\},\\ K_W(L)&=\{u:X\to Y\in W\mid p^*u\in W \text{ for every }(p:Y'\to Y)\in L\}. \end{split} \] Then $T_W(A)$ contains isomorphisms and is pullback-closed, $K_W(L)$ contains isomorphisms and is composition-closed, and \[ A\subseteq K_W(L)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad L\subseteq T_W(A). \] Both operations reverse inclusions; their composites are extensive, monotone, and idempotent. The closed pairs are exchanged by inverse order-reversing bijections.
